content: {"summary":"Payments‑api logged PAYAPI‑W0310 at ~40 /s on 18 Mar 2025 while fraud‑scorer‑01 showed only 45 % CPU because the pod was being CFS‑throttled, likely due to a thread/worker count exceeding the container CPU limit.","likely_cause":"CFS throttling caused by thread/worker count exceeding the container’s CPU limit","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"Payments‑api‑03 logged W0310 at about 40 per second while fraud‑scorer‑01 showed 30% throttled periods and only 45% average CPU.","evidence_ids":["RB-002#3"],"quote":"payments-api-03.prod.internal was logging W0310 at about 40 per second while fraud-scorer-01.prod.internal showed 30% throttled periods and only 45% average CPU"},{"text":"When p99 latency climbs while CPU looks comfortable, CFS throttling is the likely culprit.","evidence_ids":["RB-002#0"],"quote":"If a service's p99 latency climbs while its CPU graph looks comfortable, suspect CFS throttling"},{"text":"The usual trigger is a thread count sized to the node instead of the container, causing throttling despite low average CPU.","evidence_ids":["RB-002#2"],"quote":"The usual trigger is a thread count sized to the node instead of the container"}],"next_checks":["Check container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total vs container_cpu_cfs_periods_total for fraud‑scorer‑01","Inspect nr_throttled and nr_periods via kubectl exec inside the pod","Verify GOMAXPROCS (Go) and WEB_CONCURRENCY (Python) match the pod CPU limit","Confirm CPU limit and thread/worker count are aligned in the Deployment","Add a throttling alert if not already present"]}
